THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
[31st March, 1944]
An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Central
Government for the year beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944
1. Short title and extent.-(1) This Act may be called the (The word
"Indian" omitted by the Federal Laws (Revision and Declaration) Act,
1951 (26 of 1951), s. 3 and 2nd Sch.)*
Finance Act, 1944.
(Subs. by Ordinance 21 of 1960, s. 3 and
2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for the original
sub-section (2), as amended by A. O., 1949.) [(2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan.]

Fixation of salt duty

THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
[31st March, 1944]
An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Central
Government for the year beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944
2. Fixation of salt duty. The duty on salt manufactured in, or
imported by land into, (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O.,1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] shall, for the year beginning on the 1st day of April,
1944, be at the rate of one rupee and nine annas per stan dard maund.

Inland postage rates

[31st March, 1944]
An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Central
Government for the year beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944
3. Inland postage rates. For the year beginning on the 1st day of
April, 1944, the schedule contained in Schedule I to the Finance Act, 1943,
shall again be inserted in the Post Office Act, 1898, as the First Schedule to
that Act, VIII of 1943, VI of 1898.

Continuation of, and enhancement of, additional duties of customs imposed by section 6, Act XII of 1942

THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
[31st March, 1944]
An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Central
Government for the year beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944
4. Continuation of and enhancement of additional duties of customs
imposed by section 6, Act XII of 1942. -(1) The additional duties of
customs on certain goods chargeable with a duty of customs under the First
Schedule to the Tariff Act, 1934, or under the said Schedule read with any
notification of the Central Government for the time being in force, imposed up
to the 31st day of March, 1943, by section 6 of the Finance Act, 1942, and
continued up to the 31st day of March, 1944, by section 4 of the Finance Act,
1943, shall continue to be levied and collected as provided in section 6 of the
Finance Act, 1942, up to the 31st day of March, 1945, subject to the modifica tion
contained in sub-section (2), XXXII of 1934, XII of 1942, VIII of 1943, XII of
1942.
(2) The additional duty to be
levied and collected under the foregoing sub-section shall be one-half instead
of one-fifth of the amount of the duty of customs specified in the First
Schedule to the Tariff Act, 1934, in the case of the following goods, namely,
XXXII of 1934 :-
(a) spirits, comprised in Item
No. 22 (4) and in Item No. 22 (5) of the said Schedule;
(b) tobacco, comprised in Item
No. 24 and in Item No. 24 (3) of the said Schedule;
(c) cigars, comprised in Item No.
24 (1) of the said Schedule;
(d) cigarettes, comprised in Item
No. 24 (2) of the said Schedule.

sub-sections (2), (3) and
(a) income-tax for the year
beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944, shall be charged at the rates

therein in respect of each such rate of income-tax, and
(b) rates of super-tax for the

(b) where the total income of an
assessee, not being a company, includes any income chargeable under the head
"Salaries" on which super-tax has been or might have been deducted

1922, the super- tax payable by the assessee on that portion of his total
income which consists of such inclusions shall be an amount bearing to the
total amount of super-tax pay able according to the rates applicable under the
operation of the Finance Act, 1943, on his total income the same proportion as
the amount of such inclusions bears to his total income.
(3) In making any assessment for
the year ending on the 31st day of March, 1944, or the year ending on the 31st
day of March, 1945,-
(a) where the total income of a
company includes any profits and gains from life insurance business the super
tax payable by the company on that part of its total income which consists of
such inclusion shall be in the case of an assessment for the first mentioned
year at the rate of one anna and one pie in the rupee and in the case of an
assessment for the second mentioned year at the rate of nine pies in the rupee;
(b) where the total income of an
assessee, not being a company, includes any profits and gains from life
insurance business the income-tax and super-tax payable by the assessee on that
part of his total income which consists of such inclusion shall be an amount

the same proportion as the amount of such inclusion bears to his total income,

Continuance of and rate of excess profits tax

THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
THE FINANCE ACT, 1944
[31st March, 1944]
An Act to give effect to the financial proposals of the Central
Government for the year beginning on the 1st day of April, 1944
7. Continuance of and rate of excess profits tax.-(1) In sub-clause
(a) of clause (6) of section 2 of the Excess Profits Tax Act, 1940, for the
words and figures "31st day of March, 1944," the words and figures
"31st day of March, 1945," shall be substituted, XV of 1940.
(2) The excess profits tax
imposed by section 4 of the Excess Profits Tax Act, 1940, shall, in respect of
any chargeable account ing period beginning after the 31st day of March, 1944,
be an amount equal to sixty-six and two-thirds percent. of the amount by which
the profits of the business during that chargeable accounting period exceed the
standard profits, XV of 1940.
